clue.text: Plant conforming to proper standard, perhaps

parts.note: prim means proper, primly correct in manner
a standard is a shrub trained on a single upright stem, often a rose bush, so a rose is one example

explanation.surface: A gardener's specimen that meets the correct official standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' looks like a measure of quality, but in gardening a standard is a tall single-stemmed shrub, typically a rose.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale yellow spring flower of woods and hedgerows, so a kind of plant.

clue.text: His imitations may not be flattering

definitions.text: His imitations may not be flattering

parts.words: His imitations may not be flattering
parts.note: describes a person who mocks others by mimicking their style for comic effect

explanation.surface: A comment that impressions are not always complimentary.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the saying that imitation is the sincerest form of flattery.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer or performer who mimics another's style to ridicule it.

clue.text: Inn serves drunken Highlanders here

indicators.note: drunken says the letters of inn serves stagger into a different order

explanation.surface: A pub where Scottish Highlanders get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' rearranges INN SERVES. The town is the main city of the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief town of the Scottish Highlands is where many Highlanders live.

clue.text: Sort of character to take a single, then get caught

parts.note: in cricket a batsman takes a single by making a run between the wickets
I, the Roman numeral, stands for a single one
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cricketer's personality shown by scoring one then being caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket terms: a single is one run scored; 'caught' is a way of being out, written C on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Germanic letters are runes, and a rune is one kind of written letter or symbol.

clue.text: Oilcan often used round this small catch

parts.note: a tin packed with oil is the usual way small oily fish are sold

explanation.surface: A mechanic oils something small he has caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oilcan' looks like a mechanic's tool, but read as a can of oil, the tin these small fish are packed in.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fish caught at sea, commonly sold tinned in oil.

clue.text: Second best comic

parts.note: the cream is the best part, as in the cream of the crop

explanation.surface: Ranking a comedian as runner-up in a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hilarious is called a scream, so a comic person in informal speech.

clue.text: Flower clock?

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, so a timepiece worked by flowing water

explanation.surface: A clock made of blooms in a park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' means something that flows. The ancient water clock measured time by water dripping out.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient water clock measured time by the steady flow of water through a hole.

clue.text: The spirit of the English Tommy

parts.note: Tommy is a pet form of Thomas, abbreviated THOS

explanation.surface: The fighting spirit of the British soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tommy' suggests the British soldier, but it is the name Thomas, abbreviated THOS.
explanation.definitionFit: The characteristic spirit or guiding beliefs of a community or culture.

clue.text: He suffers a little from arty romantics

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone who endures a bit of suffering from artistic Romantics.
explanation.definitionFit: One who endures great pain or persecution for a cause.

clue.text: Cause infringement and get removed from goal

parts.note: off means removed or away from
end means goal, aim or purpose

explanation.surface: A footballer fouls and is sent off near the goal.
explanation.walkthrough: The footballing surface misleads: 'goal' is an aim, END.
explanation.definitionFit: To break a law or rule is to commit an infringement.

clue.text: Headless yellow bird

indicators.note: headless says the word for yellow loses its first letter

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, and craven is another word for cowardly

explanation.surface: A gruesome image of a decapitated canary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow' looks like a colour, but it means cowardly here: CRAVEN, which loses its head C.
explanation.definitionFit: A large black member of the crow family, so an example of a bird.

clue.text: Extra fee required for this course?

definitions.text: Extra fee required for this course?

parts.words: Extra fee required for this course?
parts.note: two senses joined: a further fee paid to a barrister when a case runs long, and a short course of training that brings skills up to date

explanation.surface: Asking whether a training course costs an additional payment.
explanation.walkthrough: In British law the term also names the extra daily fee paid to counsel for a long trial.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a supplementary barrister's fee and a training course that updates knowledge.

clue.text: Charge in a drinking den, say, ruined one

indicators.note: in says the following pieces go inside the word for a drinking den

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or drinking den

indicators.note: say tells us a word is spoken, so we want letters that sound like it

parts.note: ruined means wrecked
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An accusation about something being wrecked in a seedy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals sound: RECT sounds like 'wrecked' (ruined). RECT and I go inside DIVE. 'Charge' is an instruction or order, not an accusation.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge can mean an instruction given with authority, which is what an official order is.

clue.text: Sister Suzy loses her heart to effeminate boy

indicators.note: losing the heart means the middle letters of the name Suzy are dropped, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A girl called Suzy falls for a soft young lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses her heart' looks romantic but means remove the middle letters UZ of SUZY, leaving SY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated and insulting term for a weak or girlish boy.

clue.text: Recognize one side of leaf from small leek, so-called

parts.note: to see something is to recognize or perceive it
a page is one side of a leaf of a book

explanation.surface: A gardener identifying a tiny leek from part of its leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a pun: 'leek, so-called' means a word spoken like leek, so a small leak, a slow trickle.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow trickle of liquid through a gap is a minor leak.

clue.text: Putting down a cellar

parts.note: a basement is an underground storey, like a cellar

explanation.surface: Laying down a cellar beneath a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting down' suggests building a floor, but means humiliation.
explanation.definitionFit: Humiliation or degradation is the act of lowering someone in esteem.

clue.text: Fair car, good bumper

parts.note: a car at a funfair whose whole purpose is bumping into other cars

explanation.surface: Praise for a light-coloured car with a sturdy front bumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' looks like a colour or verdict on the car, but it is the funfair, and a 'good bumper' is a car that bumps well.
explanation.definitionFit: A small electric car at an amusement park, driven to collide with others.

clue.text: Drawing of a building, perhaps, but not an architect's plan

definitions.text: Drawing of a building, perhaps, but not an architect's plan

parts.words: Drawing of a building, perhaps, but not an architect's plan
parts.note: a draughtsman's view of one face of a building, as distinct from a plan, which shows it from above

explanation.surface: A sketch of a building that isn't a formal blueprint.
explanation.walkthrough: Architects distinguish the plan (a horizontal view) from the side-on view of a front or flank.
explanation.definitionFit: Architects call a flat drawing of one side of a building this, contrasted with a plan seen from above.

clue.text: French critic wearing flower is a restrained person

indicators.note: wearing says the river surrounds the critic's name like clothing

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Dee is a British river
Hippolyte Taine was a nineteenth-century French critic and historian

explanation.surface: A French critic with a flower in his buttonhole is under arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river, the DEE, which wears (holds) TAINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held in custody is a person restrained.

clue.text: Jersey's alight!

parts.note: read as 'Jersey is', then 'alight' as come down to earth, rather than on fire

explanation.surface: An alarmed cry that Jersey is on fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey is one of the Channel Islands; read the clue as IS + LAND (alight, as a bird lands).
explanation.definitionFit: Jersey is a piece of land surrounded by sea, and 'is' plus 'land' (alight) spells the word.

clue.text: The key part of Runyon's genius

indicators.note: part of says the musical key becomes part of the writer's first name, sitting inside it

parts.note: Damon was the first name of the American writer Damon Runyon
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: The essence of the American writer's brilliance.
explanation.walkthrough: Damon Runyon wrote stories of Broadway gangsters. 'genius' here is an attendant spirit, not brilliance.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical belief a genius is a guardian spirit, as is this spelling of demon.

clue.text: Dick was able to go to sea with this disability

definitions.text: Dick was able to go to sea with this disability

parts.words: Dick was able to go to sea with this disability
parts.note: names a sailor called Dick, seen as having a blind eye, and the nickname that joins the two

explanation.surface: A seaman called Dick sailed despite his handicap.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Deadeye is the sour sailor in Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera HMS Pinafore; the disability is a useless eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A blind or useless eye is the handicap, and the sailor's name in the opera contains it.

clue.text: Move a candle on south side of the choir

definitions.text: on south side of the choir

indicators.note: move says the letters of a candle are shifted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to shift a candle in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move' rearranges A CANDLE. The dean's stall is on the south side of a cathedral choir, so that side is named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: The dean's side of a cathedral choir is the south side, and this adjective means of the dean.

clue.text: Class has its buffoons

parts.note: CL is an abbreviation for class
owns means has, possesses

explanation.surface: Every school class contains a few jokers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Circus fools or jesters are comic buffoons.

clue.text: Inflamed about metric measurement

parts.note: lit means set alight, inflamed
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone getting angry over metrication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inflamed' suggests anger, but here it means set on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of volume in the metric system, so a metric measure.

clue.text: Junk-food?

parts.note: read as rubbish that is also something eaten, the stomach lining of a cow

explanation.surface: A question about unhealthy snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: Tripe is both nonsense (junk) and a cow's stomach lining eaten as food.
explanation.definitionFit: Cow's stomach lining is eaten, and the word also means worthless nonsense.

clue.text: Dish one found in Chaldean ruins

indicators.note: found in says the piece for one sits inside the rearranged letters
ruins says the letters of Chaldean are wrecked into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An archaeologist finds a bowl among ancient Babylonian ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruins' turns CHALDEAN into ENCHLADA, and 'found in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican tortilla rolled round a filling and baked in sauce is a food served as a course.

clue.text: It makes us fancy cake

parts.note: the sugar coating that turns a plain sponge into a decorated one, and that makes us want cake

explanation.surface: A remark on what makes people crave cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' works as a verb (want) and an adjective (decorated): a sweet coating does both.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugary decorative coating spread over a cake makes it ornate and tempting.

clue.text: Knock something off record

explanation.surface: A note to reduce a price and keep a log of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock something off is to reduce an asset's book value; to record is to put on paper.

clue.text: Sovereign always in circulation

parts.note: a king from Greek myth punished by being bound forever to a revolving wheel, read as if a gold coin

explanation.surface: A gold coin that is still legal tender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sovereign' looks like the British gold coin, but it is a king of Greek myth, Ixion, tied to an ever-turning fiery wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical Thessalian king was bound for eternity to a spinning wheel.

clue.text: Detective giving order to hustle

indicators.note: giving order to says the letters of hustle are put into a fresh sequence

explanation.surface: A police inspector telling someone to hurry up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving order to' looks like a command but signals rearranging HUSTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracker or investigator; the word comes from a sleuth-hound used to follow trails.

clue.text: Good taste for example, in English cut

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for example goes inside the word for cut

parts.note: to lance is to cut, as a boil
eg is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: An example of refined style is a well-tailored English suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like tailoring but is the verb LANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Refinement and grace in style or manner show discerning taste.
